title: How springs store and release energy
examples: Where does the energy go when you squash a spring?
How does a spring power a toy?
Why does a spring stop springing back?

explain.say: When you squash, stretch or twist a spring, you do work on it. That work is stored in the bent metal as elastic potential energy, ready to be given back.

draw.text: How springs store and release energy

explain.say: Let go and a good steel spring gives back almost all of it, about 95 percent or more, as motion: it pushes, pulls or turns whatever is attached.
A little energy turns into heat inside the metal as it bends, so no spring is perfect. That is why a bouncing spring slowly stops.

Stretch a spring too far, past its elastic limit, and it bends for good and stops springing back. Machines use springs to store energy for later, like a clock mainspring, or to push parts back, like a pen's click button.

faq.q: Where does the energy go when you squash a spring?
faq.a: It is stored as elastic potential energy in the bent coils of metal. When the spring is released, that energy becomes movement.
asks: What energy does a spring store?

faq.q: Does a spring give back all its energy?
faq.a: Almost. A good steel spring returns about 95 percent or more of the energy put in. The rest warms the metal a little.

faq.q: Why does a spring stop springing back?
faq.a: If you stretch it past its elastic limit, the metal bends permanently and the spring stays longer. It no longer returns to its original shape.

faq.q: How does a spring power a toy?
faq.a: Winding the key tightens a coiled spring called a mainspring. As it slowly unwinds, it turns gears that move the toy.

faq.q: What kinds of springs are there?
faq.a: Compression springs push back when squashed, tension springs pull back when stretched, torsion springs twist back, and spiral springs coil up to store energy.

facts: Elastic potential energy is stored when a material is squashed, stretched or twisted within its elastic limit.
For a spring within its limit, the stretch is proportional to the force, which is Hooke's law.

quiz.say: You stretch a spring far past its elastic limit. What happens?
quiz.show: You stretch a spring far past its elastic limit. What happens?
quiz.why: Past the elastic limit the metal bends permanently, so the spring no longer returns to its shape.

wrong.1: Energy is lost into bending the metal, not stored.
wrong.2: It springs back less, not more.
